Existing payments attached to an organization booking could therefore be exposed or acted on through personal routes. The fix rejects both provider-bound and unbound tenant payments across active-owner, viewer and suspended-member states, with zero provider calls or tenant mutations; personal access remains functional. The existing organization/D12 HTTP suite also passed.
- The original extension-notification failure was reproduced leaving a partial pending request. After the fix the equipment HTTP/DB lifecycle passed in UTC and Asia/Riyadh, including notification/audit rollback, concurrent duplicate requests and closed-rental rejection.
- Independent source reviews found no blocking defect. Required PR/main release checks must pass before merge/deployment acceptance.

deliveries.title: Bind commerce terms to verified collection and guarded refund execution
deliveries.authorDeclaredScopeAndLimits:
## Why this change is needed

Commerce decisions are now approved per service, but mutable catalog data and administrative payment labels do not preserve the original contract or prove that money was collected or refunded. A rental could reach handover without matching provider and ledger evidence, and there was no guarded provider refund execution tied to the customer's request and financial authority.

## What changes

- Freeze original booking, store-line and enrollment terms, including the supplying center, buyer, amount, currency, schedule and versioned line policy. New trip checkout requires explicit acceptance of the original quote before calling the provider. Historical contracts are not assigned new fees retroactively.
- Implement the approved trip, course, equipment-rental and eligible-goods policy boundaries. Unresolved legal classification, pre-start course cancellation charges and unconfigured original prices remain reviewable.
- Add durable refund reservations and a single dispatch claim outside retrying database transactions. Require a real customer request, independently approved existing ledger entry, active owner-approved monetary mandates and separate preparation/approval/execution actors. Cap cumulative refunds against the request, policy and capture.
- Preserve uncertain provider outcomes without automatic resend or attributing a cumulative GET total to this operation. Store validated original POST evidence for safe ledger-posting recovery. Previously observed full refunds cannot revert to captured after a stale invoice observation.
- Recover overlapping reservation unique-key conflicts only after rollback in a fresh transaction, with exact request and current mandate checks. A deterministic PostgreSQL regression reproduces the CI failure and verifies one provider request; another nonce, changed request or revoked mandate cannot use that recovery to authorize a refund.
- Add original rental handover timing, accepted hosted checkout, provider reconciliation and publication of source evidence against a posted revenue entry. Recheck collection before payment confirmation and handover. Keep the original 15-minute inventory hold and distinguish provider capture, financial reconciliation and center confirmation.
- Calculate trip entitlement only for actually performed, collected seats. Add explicit owner allocation approval/revocation bound to current evidence, and deduplicate preparation in the existing ledger. Unknown commissions are not assumed to be zero; preparation is not a bank transfer.
- Clear quote/acceptance state on identity changes and dismissals. Late asynchronous checkout responses cannot reveal a prior session's terms or redirect the next session.

## Validation

Local acceptance uses Node 22 and disposable PostgreSQL 18 with a loopback synthetic Moyasar server. It covers original-term immutability, consent before payment, personal/organization separation, partial/full refunds, concurrent requests, mandate revocation, customer-request caps, timeout after provider application, posting rollback, rental collection/handover evidence, attendance allocation and duplicate settlement prevention. Additive migrations are exercised against TEXT/UUID identity fixtures and the actual canonical schema.

CI runs those suites, the existing API regressions and full browser validation on the candidate. Browser acceptance includes checkout consent and delayed-body logout/account-switch/dismissal cases. No real payment or bank transfer is made by acceptance fixtures. Source-bound local receipts and CI results are tracked separately from production readiness.

## Migration and rollout

Four forward migrations add optional original contract fields, the operation/mandate/evidence journals, rental handover terms, and a scoped unique settlement reference. Existing rows keep null historical snapshots; no commercial rate, financial grant, tax identity or production approval is seeded. Run the normal migration/release gate and verify the deployed commit and database readiness.

## Completion boundary

This advances B01, B02, B04, B08 and the contract evidence shared with B12. It does **not** close all seven orange scopes. Fiscal profile verification and tax invoice issuance, actual center bank payout routing, remaining store/course collection and refund integration, rental refunds, complete mixed-line acceptance, wallet/reward/instructor rules, organization payment delegation and B2B procurement still require their own implementation and evidence. Insurance/damage terms remain conditional on their applicability. See `docs/center-finance/COMMERCE_POLICY_AND_EXECUTION.md`.

deliveries.title: Preserve navigation and agent consent during asynchronous refresh
deliveries.authorDeclaredScopeAndLimits:
## Why this change is needed

Main-branch browser acceptance after #663 exposed a real navigation race in the instructor portal. Opening a training view selects it immediately and starts an asynchronous reload. Its completion then selected training again unconditionally. A user who returned Home while that request was pending could be sent back to training, leaving Home controls such as the professional profile inaccessible.

The failed browser snapshot showed the earnings view still selected after the Home click. The same interleaving is reproduced by executing the existing production route handler with a deliberately deferred reload.

## What changes

- Track the workspace's existing synchronous selection event and capture its version when opening training.
- Refresh training after reload only while that selection is still current and its original element remains connected and selected.
- Preserve the normal completion refresh when the user is still viewing that training page.
- Add source-executing regressions for Home, another service, successive training selections, role/logout resets, and a detached target.
- Make the existing desktop, tablet, and mobile portal tests hold the actual earnings response until after Home is selected, await the real reload completion, and verify that Home and the professional-profile action remain usable.

## Validation

The new regression fails against the previous production source and passes with the fix. The existing navigation unit file passes all 17 cases, including its 10 earlier cases and 7 new regression cases. Syntax checks and the complete static validation step pass, including 151 unit tests and all six static validators. Full browser and API acceptance run on this pull request and again on its merged source.

## Release relationship

This is a focused follow-up to #663, based on its actual merge commit `f3aebb2713198e3cbf653e8ee81a0c32833b66aa`. The release evidence will bind both the financial implementation and this navigation correction to the final deployed commit. The financial completion boundaries documented in #663 remain applicable.

## Agent form refresh follow-up

The connected API/browser acceptance exposed a native review-checkbox click that did not change its state during the second task enqueue. Source review found that the 15-second background refresh can lock active form controls and redraw their surroundings. The original CI log did not trace the exact timer/click interleaving.

The timer now defers intrusive loading while a form field is focused, or while a focused form button retains its reason or consent. Fresh role authorization and stale-metric marking continue during that deferral. A successful form reset resumes normal polling even if the submit button keeps focus. Authorization cleanup and pending-check ownership are fenced by the current version and session.

The connected API browser fixture and its native checkbox check are unchanged. Normal loading, mutation, submission and revision checks retain their prior bodies.

Latest local verification: **159/159 source-executing unit tests plus all six static validators passed**. Against the original production source, the eight new source regressions produced one pass and seven expected assertion failures. Three deterministic clock browser cases cover active editing, polling recovery, permission revocation and stale metrics; their actual browser acceptance is being run by the existing CI workflows.

The branch also incorporates the independently merged PR665 and PR667 test changes without attributing them to this fix. All 1,683 source blobs match the published candidate tree.

## Latest concurrent UTC correction

The branch now also integrates independently merged PR669 (`0f56498f3090e7631dac7e6fe2580d3868e5b2c4`): explicit UTC operational timestamps and their Asia/Riyadh database regression. Its changes build on PR667’s isolated rollback acceptance; overlapping files retain PR669’s latest contents. The six authored UI files remain unchanged from the preceding candidate. The complete 1,683-blob combined source was verified against tree `6a9c3033b148295ec6ec144e887ed3c4c715538a`; this combined source is being evaluated by its own current CI run.

deliveries.title: Center invoice controls, completed-trip histories and private provider payout profiles
deliveries.authorDeclaredScopeAndLimits:
Center accounts open vessel bookings, bind the chosen vessel to the supplying center, and attach the customer's original invoice. Instructors and marine operators cannot issue or upload a separate service invoice. Existing signed compensation agreements and earnings are untouched. Archived PDFs retain their original issuer and are not reassigned.

Center managers can request opening or closing center invoicing separately for courses and boat trips. Platform finance reviews the request. Center billing starts enabled to preserve previously available center billing. An approval never gives an instructor or a boat operator permission to invoice. The center print view opens the stored PDF. The trip issuer and selected vessel are captured at booking. Previously open center boat trips without a recorded vessel require the center to select one before new bookings.

Verification: API build, 24 PostgreSQL checkout, invoice and trip history cases, 159 web tests and 13 Chromium scenarios. Chromium verified the printable PDF matches the original bytes. No physical printer, real payment or real customer booking was used.

Boat operators and instructors now see a paginated completed-trip history. Marine totals count recorded passenger attendances. Instructor totals count distinct students across completed teaching sessions. Completed trips are counted once per role even with multiple bookings or students.

The instructor and marine owner profiles now show a private editor for mobile, contact email, emergency phone, optional emergency contact name and a Saudi payout IBAN. Existing contact values prefill. Changing the contact email leaves the login email intact. Bank changes are encrypted per beneficiary and never returned by the self-profile read. An active accountant in the linked center can explicitly retrieve an eligible payee's bank details, with audit and no-store responses.

The current revision passed the API build, the 25-case PostgreSQL/HTTP acceptance suite, the TEXT and UUID booking-search fixtures, 159 web unit tests and focused Chromium tests for both roles. deliveries.title: B12: finalize organization invoices and confirm center transfer receipts
deliveries.authorDeclaredScopeAndLimits:
## Why
Organization booking payment currently stops at a draft invoice, while center entitlements stop at an approval draft. Attaching a seller PDF does not finalize its invoice, and the general ledger intentionally cannot post a center entitlement without transfer evidence. This completes those B12 technical paths while retaining the published prepayment, delegation and collection safeguards.

## Changes
- Let the supplying center accountant review and finalize its original invoice, preserving seller/buyer snapshots, the original document hash, source contract and matched posted collection. Seller numbering stays scoped to its center; the platform reference remains unique.
- Record an already executed external center transfer, then require a separate incoming-bank PDF and confirmation from a center accountant independent of the requester, approver and submitter before posting the settlement.
- Recheck service execution, current collection, allocation and refund evidence inside serializable transactions; retain rejected proofs and prevent duplicate posting or reuse of a bank reference for another settlement.
- Add the invoice review UI and one shared transfer workspace for the platform owner and center accountant, including stale-session and failure handling.
- Queue organizational invoice notices after final approval. Defer older draft email rows before budget reservation or transport; preserve issued legacy, personal and store invoice behavior.
- Add forward-only evidence tables and targeted database, HTTP and browser coverage to the existing CI gates.

## Verification
- API typecheck, lint and build; controller route uniqueness; unchanged production migration checksums.
- Existing organization mandate/prepayment PostgreSQL acceptance, extended through final invoice approval, original PDF byte readback, idempotency, immutable party snapshots and revoked membership.
- 15 center-transfer checks: 14 financial service cases and one real HTTP flow with scrypt login, sessions, AccessTokenGuard, invoice finalization and independent transfer confirmation. Includes concurrent requests, refund/allocation changes and rollback after ledger mutation.
- Forward migration tested with both TEXT and UUID source identities, repeat application and seller-local numbering.
- PostgreSQL invoice notice acceptance: draft upload queues nothing; finalization queues once; repeated approval does not duplicate; legacy draft delivery waits without provider/budget use and resumes the same row.
- Focused Playwright coverage for invoice finalization, center transfers, real admin entry and existing finance/invoice behavior; web validators and unit tests.

## Operational boundary
This accepts an original invoice issued by the center and independently reviewed evidence of an external bank transfer. It does not generate tax-certified originals or dispatch funds through a bank API. Acceptance fixtures are synthetic and loopback-only; no live payment, bank transfer or email is performed. First real center-invoice and received-transfer evidence is a separate operational acceptance event, not inferred from these tests.

Tracking: [B12 / HYD-25](https://linear.app/hydroland/issue/HYD-25).

deliveries.title: B08: complete mixed orders, invoices, refunds and center settlement
deliveries.authorDeclaredScopeAndLimits:
## Why

The store could not create one order from goods, a trip, a course and equipment rental: its existing order route treated all selections as goods. Goods from multiple supplying centers also could not use the single-source checkout. Separate payment/refund flows existed, but the mixed order had no complete invoice and supplier-settlement acceptance.

## What changes

- Add an atomic customer order that links the original native records, grouping goods by supplying center and rentals by center/time window. A stable request fingerprint prevents duplicate reservations. Payment remains `PER_SOURCE`, with each source's original quote, policy and checkout.
- Display verified collection, refund, net and remaining totals from the existing ledgers. Conflicting proof returns review/unknown amounts. Add the mixed cart and route goods-only carts from multiple centers through the same grouping.
- Finalize original supplier invoices with explicit per-line tax, exact document/contract bindings and native invoice validation. Prepare supplier entitlements only from verified collection and actual service completion, with explicit owner-approved deductions.
- Record external transfer evidence and require independent incoming-receipt confirmation before posting. Protect the generic ledger routes, reject stale evidence and share bank-reference exclusion with B12.
- Add source-finance interfaces for center accountants and the owner, additive migrations, and a full PostgreSQL/Nest HTTP acceptance gate.

## Verified locally

- **27/27** mixed-order acceptance cases on a fresh UTC PostgreSQL database, actual Nest HTTP/authentication and a loopback synthetic provider, with both forward migrations applied.
- Completed order: 12,600 minor units collected, 1,200 goods refund, 11,400 eligible gross, 400 explicitly approved commission and 11,000 independently confirmed synthetic receipt.
- Cancelled order: 9,350 refunded from 12,600 collected; the retained 3,250 never becomes entitlement for unperformed sources.
- The unchanged native contract database suite **7/7**, including the serializable-retry identity regression; mixed-order retries also preserve identities and recheck changed prices for all four source types.
- Explicit taxable course invoice: 3,000 subtotal + 400 tax = 3,400 original gross, while previously finalized exempt invoices retain their original snapshots.
- TEXT/UUID migration compatibility, replay after checkless schema bootstrap, preserved history and database uniqueness/check constraints.
- Existing B12 transfer acceptance **15/15**, original policy/contract/entitlement checks **38/38**, store payment boundaries **24/24**.
- Focused browser acceptance **66/66**, followed by the two affected multi-center/single-center routing cases **2/2**; web unit tests **159/159** and six web validation gates. The two new browser specs add **21 cases** to CI.
- API build/type checking, correctness lint and route-signature uniqueness passed. Node 22 and the complete repository release gates run on this PR.

## Boundaries and release

The grouping creates no new balance ledger and no single combined payment. Seller tax and commission are explicit inputs; the platform does not invent them. Transfer records describe an externally executed transfer, and only an independent receipt review posts the ledger. Tests use synthetic evidence and execute no real charge or bank transfer.

Historical applied migrations and existing contracts remain unchanged. The B12 organization workflow stays in place. The first real mixed transaction remains operational evidence; Q01 stays last in the agreed sequence.

See [B08 acceptance and reproducible evidence](docs/B08_MIXED_COMMERCE_ACCEPTANCE.md). The change is merged and deployed; exact release and live-verification evidence follows.

## Release verification — 26 November 2026

Merged as `758e24c4752e31b1b3d3d3be2d7af243cbfab0ef`; the merged tree `b339be2eb126ad4e6f6db83c94418163d1eadba1` exactly matches the tested candidate.

- **22/22 PR workflows** and **31/31 main push workflows** succeeded. On main, 37 check runs succeeded; the existing schedule/workflow-dispatch-only `monitor-liveness` job was correctly not applicable to a push.
- [Main API validation](https://github.com/sultanasiri001-sys/hydroland/actions/runs/45822372529): **123/123 successful steps** on **Node 22.23.5**, including **27/27 B08** and **7/7 unchanged native contract checks**.

- Native Orca on main passed Arabic and English on its **first attempt**, with 26 genuine speech observations across the seven portals and six search fields. The PR's single Orca-only retry followed a recorded late native-focus/speech race; source, assertions, timeouts and PCM thresholds stayed unchanged during that retry.
- [Full release evidence gate](https://github.com/sultanasiri001-sys/hydroland/actions/runs/45822372531) succeeded on the exact main push.

deliveries.authorDeclaredScopeAndLimits:
## Why

F08 previously retained procurement preferences and representative references, but an organization could not execute a scoped supplier → purchase order → invoice → receipt → settlement → reversal/recovery cycle with independent evidence acceptance.

## What changes

- Adds organization-owned procurement contracts and orders, named person-level mandates, independent recommendation/owner decisions, partial receipts, exact invoice matching and original-PDF evidence.
- Reuses the native document creation/approval/signature lifecycle and native finance journals. Supplier invoice identity is claimed once per organization. Payment confirmation and incoming recovery use separate independent authority and preserve original journals.
- Adds serializable, idempotent commands, revision/event/audit evidence, current source and membership revalidation, and read-only review states for broken evidence.
- Prevents generic finance routes from creating or advancing procurement entries. Shares bank-reference locking and duplicate-claim checks with B08 and B12 in both directions.
- Adds an Arabic/English organization workspace with guided document drafts, explicit commercial choices, current scoped actions, original PDFs and source-safe retries.
- Adds an additive migration compatible with historical TEXT/UUID identities, isolated HTTP/PostgreSQL acceptance, native PostgreSQL dump/restore/replay evidence, and browser regressions.

## Verification before this PR

- API build and lint passed.
- Actual HTTP/controller/service/PostgreSQL acceptance: **37/37 passed**, zero failures or skipped checks, with real native document lifecycle in isolated synthetic organizations.
- Migration on TEXT and UUID originals, checkless bootstrap and repeated forward replay passed.
- B08: **27/27**; B12: **16/16**, including reciprocal F08 bank-reference guards.
- Web unit tests: **162/162** plus all static validations; production build passed.
- F08 browser scenarios: **16/16**; existing organization portal: **29/29**.

The required workflows still need to pass on this exact PR revision. The new API gate performs native `pg_dump`/`pg_restore` against its disposable PostgreSQL 18 service and retains JSON evidence.

## Acceptance boundary

All fixture identities, orders, attachments and acceptance records are synthetic. No bank/provider call or production financial test is made. The contract supports full-order settlement and full-order reversal/recovery; its agreed tax, cancellation and integration choices remain explicit. No external integration endpoint or official approval is invented, and Zid is not connected.

Final order acceptance does **not** grant F08.01/D19 project closure. Real organization, authorized representative, agreed contract/integration scope and separate representative acceptance remain required. HYD-65 therefore remains in progress pending that real acceptance.

deliveries.title: Fix F08 release warehouse race and browser CI scheduling
deliveries.authorDeclaredScopeAndLimits:
## Why
The main Web gate for F08 preparation (#718, commit c127c4b5) caught a real warehouse interaction race: a delayed profile refresh for the same signed-in account closed the warehouse dialog while the custodian was entering a partial return. The full run completed 917 tests and failed this one case.

## Changes
- Recheck warehouse access after a profile refresh while preserving the open form when authority and workspace data are unchanged.
- Separate lifecycle invalidation, GET ordering and POST ownership. A late read or an old account's POST cannot repaint or unlock newer work.
- Preserve the saved confirmation through overlapping reconciliation reads, and rebuild completed or manually refreshed forms normally.
- Clear immediately when the account, authority, portal or session changes, or current server access is refused.
- Add five deterministic browser regression cases; retain the original failing test unchanged.

## Validation
- Reproduced the old close path for the same account and session.
- Warehouse browser tests: 8/8, zero skips or retries; traces retained.
- Web unit tests: 162/162; all six static validators passed.
- Production web build, syntax checks and git diff check passed.
- Independent source review passed.

This corrects the release blockers for F08. The API and all test assertions/timeouts are unchanged. Full PR/main CI and matching live deployment verification still gate technical closure; real organization connection and human acceptance remain separate.

## Browser CI scheduling correction
The first run of this PR logged all 923 browser tests passed, then reached the existing 35-minute overall job limit before JSON verification and complete evidence retention. That cancelled run is not being treated as release evidence.

Move the 15 existing focused groups to a parallel, mandatory `focused-regressions` job. Keep `validate` for static/build checks, the four center-search cases and their JSON evidence, and the full suite with its existing verified artifact and screenshots. Record and retain the focused job's source before and after execution as explicitly source-only receipts.

All 34 original steps and commands remain; job limits remain 35/35/40 minutes and individual tests remain 30 seconds. A02 still requires all 28 workflows and now requires 33 jobs, including every focused group and its source checks. The reviewed inventory digest is re-pinned without changing evaluator logic.

Local validation: 397/397 A02 contracts and 6/6 browser-evidence contracts. Three new negative controls prove that a successful full suite cannot substitute for a missing, cancelled or skipped focused job. Independent review passed. The published head must still pass complete CI.
